title: Product-space $L^p$ quantity
statement: For a finite set $\Omega$, a probability mass function $\pi$ on $\Omega$, a natural number $n$, a real number $p$, and a real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$, define its product-space $L^p$ quantity to be the probability-weighted $L^p$ quantity under the independent product distribution with marginal $\pi$ at each coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
